transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-11-20 15:00 PST | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Gomez (Lifeline Head of AI), Samir Patel (Eng Manager), Tara Nguyen (Security)

Summary: quick sync to finalize quality evaluation plan for the POC - what we measure, what datasets we need, and timelines.

[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick roll call: alex and priya from our side.
[00:08] Dr. Maria Gomez (Lifeline): hi all, maria here. excited to map this out.
[00:12] Samir Patel: samir here.
[00:15] Tara Nguyen: tara on compliance.
[00:17] Priya Nair (Redwood): great. goal today is to lock the quality eval plan - golden prompts, regression checks, hallucination metrics and how we'll score. also confirm data and timeline.

[00:35] Alex (Redwood): quick context - Lifeline's use case is clinical note summarization + structured extraction for downstream CDS, right? we heard that the main goals are accuracy on key fields, low hallucination on PHI-like content and consistent formatting for EHR ingest. is that fair?
[00:50] Dr. Maria: yep that's right. additionally we need the output to map cleanly to our FHIR fields; format consistency is huge.
[01:03] Samir: and performance wise we care about 200 qps peak for batch during peak hours, avg 20 qps off-peak. latency target is sub-800ms for 90th percentile on the POC model. these numbers are ballpark but we need to test.

[01:25] Priya (Redwood): good, that gives us targets. for the quality eval plan we propose a layered approach: 1) golden prompt set — curated examples with expected outputs, 2) regression suite - pairs of prompts to validate previously passing cases, 3) hallucination checks - heuristics and token-level detection plus manual adjudication sample, 4) format validation - schema checks to ensure FHIR mapping, 5) scoring - composite metric combining field-exact match, BLEU-like token overlap, and hallucination penalty.
[01:54] Dr. Maria: can you expand on the composite scoring? how do you weight fields vs overall fluency?

[02:05] Priya: sure. we typically weight structured fields higher because false positives on, say, medication or allergy is expensive. example default weights: 70% structured-field f1 (per-field micro-averaged), 20% format compliance (schema pass rate), 10% free-text quality (ROUGE/BLEU proxy). hallucinations get an explicit negative penalty — any hallucinated PHI-like insertion reduces the composite by a fixed fraction, and we flag for manual review.

[02:35] Samir: ok that makes sense. how does manual adjudication fit in? sounds expensive.

[02:42] Priya: we run automated detectors first — e.g., unexpected entity insertion compared to patient record — then sample N items for human review. for the POC we recommend 500 golden+test records and a 5% manual sample for hallucination adjudication. that keeps costs in check while giving signal.

[03:05] Tara (Security): quick pause — anything involving PHI needs to be de-identified for the hosted benchmark, unless we go Private with our VPC and KMS. what's Redwood's recommendation?

[03:18] Alex: recommend first run on Redwood hosted with de-identified data; if results are promising we'll move to Dedicated or Private for a second run with stronger controls. we support KMS integrations and audit logs for Private.

[03:33] Dr. Maria: timeline? we'd like an initial benchmark in two weeks. is that feasible?

[03:38] Priya: yes if we get the 500 de-identified samples by next Thursday (2025-11-27). we can seed golden prompts off those and run the hosted bench week of 2025-12-01.

[03:56] Alex: to confirm the success criteria — proposed go/no-go: >= 0.88 composite score on the POC dataset, <1% hallucination rate on sampled adjudication, and 90th percentile latency < 800ms on target config. does that align?
[04:16] Samir: the composite 0.88 feels ambitious but we'll take it as target; can we define a fallback? like if we hit 0.82 we move to quantized slower model plus more prompt engineering?
[04:30] Priya: yes we'll include model variants and quantization profiles in the bench. Redwood Optimize will provide suggestions for batching and quant params tied to workload. fallback plan is part of the deliverable.

[04:45] Dr. Maria: also need regression tests for future model updates — we can't have silent drift. what's your recommended cadence?
[04:54] Priya: recommend running the regression suite on every model change and weekly during the pilot. regression suite will include our golden prompts plus customer-submitted critical examples. any regression beyond threshold triggers rollback or canary.

[05:10] Alex: let's talk about golden prompts: we will craft ~50 gold examples that cover edge cases — negations, multiple medications, truncated notes, misspellings, etc. you'll review and approve them. golden set will be locked for the POC evaluation.

[05:28] Dr. Maria: can we include clinician-authored edge cases? we can have two SMEs annotate 30 examples to seed the golden set.
[05:35] Priya: perfect. we'll combine those with 20 system-generated corner cases.

[05:42] Samir: how about metrics instrumentation? we need per-field breakdowns and token-level logs for debugging.
[05:48] Priya: Redwood Console will provide per-field accuracy, per-route latency, token counts and error traces. for debugging we'll provide sample traces with request/response and KV cache stats if relevant. some fields may be obfuscated in logs for PHI.

[06:05] Tara: about logs — we need audit logs that show who accessed what outputs and key rotation details for KMS. can Redwood provide SOC2 artifact mapping?
[06:15] Alex: yes, we have SOC2 docs and a Private deployment checklist mapping controls to artifacts. we'll share those. for hosted benches we'll restrict logs and can provide redacted traces.

[06:28] Dr. Maria: scoring details — can you show an example scoring sheet?
[06:33] Priya: sure. example scoring for a record: structured fields (binary exact match per field) -> compute per-field precision/recall -> F1 aggregated; format pass/fail for JSON schema; free text quality score via ROUGE-L normalized; hallucination flag boolean. final composite as weighted sum. we'll attach an example spreadsheet.

[06:55] Samir: what's your approach to hallucination detection automation?

[06:59] Priya: a mix — entity overlap with patient record, external knowledge consistency checks, and model-level uncertainty heuristics (e.g., low probability spans). those heuristics surface candidates and then manual sample adjudication confirms. false positive rate of the detector is possible so manual sample helps calibrate.

[07:18] Dr. Maria: for format validation, can you enforce strict schema output? we need consistent enums for certain fields.
[07:25] Priya: yes we run a schema validator post-response; failures get counted into format compliance. we can also provide a strict mode where the model is prompted to output JSON only; fallback is to run lightweight post-processing to coerce. strict mode reduces hallucination risk but may increase latency slightly.

[07:43] Alex: on the workload sizing — Samir you mentioned peak 200 qps. can you confirm concurrency and average tokens per request?
[07:50] Samir: typical note size is 600-900 tokens, average ~750. extraction responses are concise, ~80-120 tokens. concurrency peak estimate 40 concurrent workers issuing requests - aligns to the 200 qps estimate.

[08:10] Priya: that'll inform batching and memory. for 750-token context we may pick a model variant that balances LLM throughput and quantization profile. we'll run latency bench for the three suggested variants: 1) FP16 large model, 2) 4-bit quantized optimized, 3) distilled smaller model.

[08:30] Samir: can you run the benches under our typical payload distribution (70% extract+format, 30% long summary)?
[08:36] Priya: yes we'll simulate that mix. please include any edge-case heavy time windows if you have them.

[08:45] Dr. Maria: about cost estimate for hosted bench and pilot — what's the expected bill for the POC run?
[08:52] Alex: for the hosted benchmark run + 2 weeks pilot, rough estimate $6k- $12k depending on model selection and token volumes. we'll provide line items in the SOW.
